transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Avery, Rohit, Sofia, Jake (Redwood); Lina, Markus, Priya, Devon, Hana (OrbitEdge)
---
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Lina (OrbitEdge): Lina here, hi.
[00:08] Markus (OrbitEdge): Markus.
[00:09] Priya (OrbitEdge): Priya on product.
[00:11] Devon (OrbitEdge): Devon, security.
[00:13] Hana (OrbitEdge): Hana, ops.
[00:15] Avery: Great. Rohit and Sofia from our side too, and Jake for the listing questions. We're here to map the technical plan for Marketplace + ref-arch. I'll kick off with objectives.
[00:30] Rohit (Redwood SE): Quick FYI, I'll focus more on the infra pieces — packaging, KV cache behavior, autoscaling.
[00:36] Sofia (Redwood PE): I'll cover partner engineering handoffs for the listing assets.
[00:40] 
Summary / Context
[00:45] Avery: OrbitEdge wants a joint solution tile on AWS Marketplace that references Redwood Dedicated and an OrbitEdge managed offering. Primary constraints were data residency and wanting a VPC-first deployment model. You mentioned wanting a vendor-backed listing and also an option for customers to bring their own license, Lina?
[01:00] Lina: Yeah — two SKU approach ideally. One is fully managed with OrbitEdge + Redwood running in OrbitEdge's managed tenancy, second is BYOL for enterprise customers who want to host themselves.
[01:12] Priya: Timeline is tight — marketing asked for a draft listing by the end of May to align with our partner launch on June 10th.
[01:20] Avery: OK good, we'll try to align.

Topics covered and technical notes
[01:30] Markus: From a technical perspective we have two main questions: how do we package the Redwood runtime for Marketplace (AMI versus container), and what the networking looks like for VPC peering or PrivateLink?
[01:40] Rohit: For low-op friction, container + helm chart works well — but AWS Marketplace AMI flow is often required for some partners that want a machine image. We can support both: provide an AMI build and a helm chart helm snippets. Our runtime supports k8s deployment and also AMI-backed single-tenant images.
[01:58] Hana: Our CI/CD currently pushes to an internal ECR and we have strict image signing — any AMI build needs to accept signed artifacts.
[02:06] Jake (Redwood): We should document the registry requirements. We'll add an example workflow.
[02:12] Rohit: Note about the runtime: when deployed in Dedicated mode inside a VPC we recommend certain kernel parameters and hugepages for GPU hosts; plus KV cache needs a sticky local volume for perf — that's a gotcha if the Marketplace installation uses ephemeral storage.
[02:30] Markus: Sticky local volumes — ok, we can map a persistent EBS or EFS. Good call.

[02:40] Priya: Can you explain the billing / metering piece for Marketplace? How does consumption get reported?
[02:45] Sofia: On AWS Marketplace you can do SaaS metering or AMI with BYOL. For SaaS, there's a direct metering API call pattern where our control plane can emit usage events; for AMI/Marketplace private listings we usually do an offline reconciliation via license keys. Depends on the SKU.
[03:05] Lina: We want per-request token metering ideally so customers see cost correlations. Is there a standard implementation?
[03:12] Rohit: We'll instrument usage emission at the request layer — the runtime can publish metering events to an ingestion endpoint. For strict offline (no egress) we can do periodic counters that OrbitEdge pulls from a metrics endpoint. There's a small delta risk but acceptable for enterprise.

Security / Compliance thread
[03:30] Devon: SOC2 and especially KMS integration are blockers for some of our customers. We need to ensure keys remain in our KMS and Redwood can integrate with customer-managed KMS via proper IAM roles.
[03:45] Rohit: We support customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) for model artifacts and for encrypting persistent caches. In private deployments we can bind to an external KMS and we use envelope encryption. Might be transcribed as K-M-S or Sam-L sometimes — apologies for the audio.
[03:58] Devon: Audit logs? We need per-request logs forwarded to our SIEM, and immutable audit entries.
[04:05] Jake: Console has token-level tracing; for private deployments we can forward logs via syslog or cloudwatch; we'll produce an example log-forwarding template.

Integration verification and tests
[04:20] Priya: What's the minimal smoke test we should run before listing?
[04:25] Rohit: Minimal: deploy helm chart in a staging VPC with a saved model, run a 1k token load test to verify latency and KV cache persistence, validate KMS key rotation, and test metering emission. We'll provide a test harness.
[04:40] Markus: Can you also verify autoscaling behavior across burst windows? We saw token spikes during demo days.
[04:46] Rohit: Yes — we'll include a synthetic traffic generator that simulates bursty token patterns. There are some caveats with batching: larger batch sizes help cost but increase p95 latency. We'll surface recommended batch policies in the ref-arch.

Artifacts referenced
[04:58] Sofia: We'll share two docs: 1) Marketplace listing checklist and 2) reference-architecture diagram with helm examples. Links to both will be in the follow-up.
[05:08] Avery: Also we'll put up a short demo video of the deployment flow — lightweight.
[05:12] Lina: Great.

Operational responsibilities and handoffs
[05:15] Hana: Who owns AMI builds and security vetting? OrbitEdge or Redwood?
[05:20] Avery: Redwood can produce the AMI build and sign it; OrbitEdge will handle the final validation in your lab account and publish. For the helm chart, Redwood maintains upstream chart and OrbitEdge will fork for any customizations needed for your marketplace SKU.
[05:32] Priya: What about support tiers — will Redwood be on the hook for L2?
[05:36] Jake: For joint listings we usually do co-supported model: OrbitEdge L1 and orchestration, Redwood L2 for runtime issues. We can formalize in the partner playbook but that is typical.

Questions from OrbitEdge
[05:48] Lina: If we do BYOL, how does license key rotation work for long-running customers?
[05:55] Rohit: We have a license service that supports rotation and TTL — keys can be bound to instance IDs or to a Kubernetes cluster fingerprint. We'll demo the rotation as part of the smoke test.
[06:06] Devon: Any network considerations for PrivateLink vs VPC peering? Our security policy favors PrivateLink.
[06:12] Rohit: PrivateLink is good for control-plane level communications; for high-throughput inference traffic, VPC peering or a managed transit gateway is better because PrivateLink can get costly at scale. We'll add a small decision matrix in the ref-arch.

Pricing and SKU engineering
[06:28] Priya: For the managed SKU we want per-token tiers; what's the best way to surface that?
[06:33] Sofia: Two options: use SaaS metering on Marketplace which pushes usage to AWS for billing, or use Marketplace listing for software and have OrbitEdge bill separately. For tight integration the SaaS metering gives best customer UX. If you need to control discounts and custom pricing, BYOL with OrbitEdge billing may be easier.
[06:52] Lina: Marketing prefers the SaaS metering option for frictionless purchase.

Timeline and milestones
[07:00] Avery: Proposed milestones: Week 1 (this week): reference-arch draft + listing checklist. Week 2: helm/AMI artifacts and smoke test in OrbitEdge staging. Week 3: finalize marketplace assets and submit listing for review. That gets us to the June window if there are no major rejections.
[07:18] Priya: Sounds good; if we hit a compliance snag it could add extra weeks.

Wrap and next steps recap
[07:25] Avery: Recap — Redwood will produce ref-arch diagram, helm snippets, AMI build process doc, smoke test harness, and security packet. OrbitEdge will provide marketplace creative, CI/CD constraints and run the verification in staging.
[07:40] Markus: We'll also confirm test account quotas with AWS.
[07:43] Hana: And we'll share our image signing policy.
[07:46] Avery: Perfect. We'll follow up with a Drive folder and the timeline.

Noise / transcription glitches (natural)
[07:52] (speaker overlap)
[07:54] Devon: — when you say K-V cache, do you mean the kay vee cache that holds previous tokens?
[07:58] Rohit: Yes, Kay vee, kv, same. Also note the cache persists to the attached EBS or local NVMe depending on instance class.

End of meeting
[08:10] Avery: Thanks everyone, we'll send the notes and action items.
[08:13] Lina: Thanks, bye.
[08:15] Priya: Bye.
---
Notes: Transcript contains small recognition errors (K-M-S, kay vee cache) and occasional speaker overlaps — follow-up doc will be authoritative for configs.
